agent_final_message:
Rewrote `snapshot/ignore.py` as a pure-Python gitignore implementation:

- `_walk` descends the tree, loading `.gitignore` patterns at each level (deeper patterns stack on top of parent patterns). Skips `.git` directly under root to match the previous behavior.
- When a directory matches an ignore pattern, `_collect_all` enumerates every file inside without applying further patterns — this correctly reproduces git's "cannot re-include files whose parent directory is excluded" rule.
- `_parse_line` handles comments, blank lines, trailing-whitespace stripping (respecting `\ ` escapes), `!` negation, `\#` / `\!` literal escapes, trailing-slash directory-only patterns, and leading-slash / leading-`**/` anchoring semantics.
- `_glob_to_regex` translates each pattern to a full-match regex, handling `*`, `?`, `[...]` (with `!`/`^` negation and `\` escapes), and the three standalone forms of `**` (leading `**/`, middle `/**/`, trailing `/**`). Non-anchored patterns get a `(?:[^/]*/)*` prefix so they match at any depth. Symlinked `.gitignore` files are ignored (matches git's behavior).
- `_is_ignored` walks the pattern stack in order, letting the last matching pattern win.

Verified against git with:
- Original 11 unit tests — pass.
- 24 hand-crafted edge cases (negation inside/outside excluded dirs, `**` positions, character classes incl. ranges and negation, trailing-space escapes, hash/bang escapes, nested overrides, dir-only vs file, etc.) — all match.
- 4 symlink cases (dir symlink, file symlink, broken symlink, dangling target, symlinked `.gitignore`) — all match.
- ~18,000 randomly generated trees across varied patterns — zero mismatches.
